title: Ex-China heavy rare earths up: Q3 2026 Rare Earths Price Review
gist: In Q3 2026, ex-China heavy rare earth prices (dysprosium, terbium, yttrium) soared while light rare earths (PrNd) stayed flat in China and fell below the $110/kg US DoD price floor ex-China. Dysprosium oxide CIF Europe reached about 16.3x the China domestic price. Benchmark expects the bifurcation to persist, with the November expiry of China's export controls and demand from new magnet makers as the Q4 catalysts.

themes.theme: China vs ex-China heavy RE bifurcation

insights.claim: Dysprosium oxide CIF Europe prices rose 150% in Q3 2026 and now trade around 16.3 times DDP China levels, up from 6.8 times at the end of Q2 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The ex-China premium for heavy rare earths more than doubled in one quarter, which makes non-Chinese Dy producers and recyclers much more attractive economically.
insights.quote: CIF Europe dysprosium oxide prices are now around 16.3 times DDP China price levels, up from 6.8 times at the end of Q2.
insights.locator: How wide did heavy rare earth price bifurcation get in Q3?

insights.claim: Yttrium oxide CIF North America trades at roughly 196 times the equivalent DDP China price, the most extreme China/ex-China spread among the rare earths.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: An almost 200x price spread shows how fragmented the yttrium market is. Arbitrage and new ex-China supply are the setups to watch.
insights.quote: the CIF North America price sits at roughly 196 times the equivalent DDP China price
insights.locator: How wide did heavy rare earth price bifurcation get in Q3?

insights.claim: Benchmark's forecasting team expects the China/ex-China heavy rare earth price bifurcation to persist, because the ex-China dysprosium-terbium premium is the economic signal needed to bring new heavy rare earth capacity online.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Do not bet on the ex-China DyTb premium mean-reverting soon. Benchmark treats it as structural until new non-China capacity arrives.
insights.quote: the ex-China DyTb premium is still the economic signal required to bring new heavy rare earth capacity online

insights.claim: Ex-China heavy rare earth supply chains remain acutely under-supplied relative to demand, and Chinese export restrictions are forcing buyers to pay significant premiums to secure larger volumes of dysprosium and terbium.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Chinese export policy directly sets the scarcity premium in Western heavy rare earths. Treat export-control news as a price catalyst.
insights.quote: There is mounting evidence that ex-China heavy rare earth supply chains remain acutely under-supplied relative to demand

insights.claim: In September 2026, dysprosium oxide CIF Europe rose 56% to an average of $3,500/kg and terbium oxide rose 23% to $6,745/kg, driven by premiums on larger-volume transactions, while Chinese domestic Dy and Tb prices kept retreating from their mid-Q3 highs.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: These are hard price levels for pricing ex-China heavy rare earth offtakes. Note that prices in the two regions moved in opposite directions.
insights.locator: By September, dysprosium oxide CIF Europe

insights.claim: In August 2026, dysprosium oxide CIF Europe rose more than 32%, terbium oxide CIF Europe rose 10% and yttrium oxide CIF North America rose nearly 18%, while Chinese domestic Dy and Tb eased slightly. In July, dysprosium oxide CIF Europe had already climbed more than 16%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Ex-China heavy rare earth prices climbed faster each month through the quarter (16%, then 32%, then 56% for Dy), a sign of a scarcity squeeze rather than a one-off spike.
insights.locator: In August, ex-China heavy rare earths rose

insights.claim: Yttrium oxide prices held steady in both China and North America in September 2026 because ongoing US production limited further upward momentum.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Even a small amount of domestic ex-China supply can cap price spikes in a rare earth element. That is a risk for anyone betting on a heavy RE element with nascent US output.

themes.theme: PrNd oversupply and the DoD price floor

insights.claim: Ex-China PrNd oxide prices (CIF North America and Europe) fell below the $110/kg floor built into MP Materials' and Lynas Rare Earths' agreements with the US Department of Defense during Q3 2026, while the China DDP price eased only 1%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: With market prices below the floor, the DoD price-floor mechanism is now in play, so MP's and Lynas's realized PrNd pricing depends on the government backstop rather than the spot market.
insights.locator: Light and heavy rare earth prices diverged

insights.claim: In August 2026, ex-China PrNd oxide prices fell more than 13%, including a 7.3% drop between 6 and 20 August. Ex-China producers, wary of the reputational risk of selling into China, redirected volume to an increasingly oversupplied ex-China market.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Political and reputational pressure to decouple from China is flooding the Western PrNd market. That depresses ex-China light rare earth prices, which is the opposite of what happens with heavy rare earths.
insights.quote: ex-China producers, wary of the reputational sensitivity of selling into China, redirected volume toward an increasingly oversupplied ex-China market
insights.locator: What happened to PrNd oxide prices in Q3?

insights.claim: Chinese domestic PrNd oxide now trades at a premium to ex-China PrNd, reversing the heavy rare earth pattern. In September 2026, China PrNd averaged RMB729,500/t (about US$108,696/t) and ex-China PrNd rose 12% to $106,500/t CIF.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Light rare earths are priced higher inside China while heavy rare earths are priced higher outside it, so a single 'Western premium' view of rare earths is wrong.
insights.quote: Chinese domestic PrNd, now commanding a premium, fell a more moderate 5% over the same month.
insights.locator: PrNd prices stabilised in China by September

insights.claim: Light rare earths outside China remain oversupplied, although Benchmark says this dynamic is stabilising after the September 2026 rebound in ex-China PrNd prices.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The fall in ex-China PrNd prices may be bottoming. Watch whether prices recover back above the $110/kg DoD floor.
insights.quote: Light rare earths beyond China remained oversupplied, though this dynamic is stabilising.

insights.claim: A US presidential determination moved to treat recoverable rare earths and end-of-life magnets as strategic defence resources, which could improve future domestic access to secondary dysprosium and terbium feedstock.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: This is a policy tailwind for US magnet-recycling and secondary-feedstock businesses as a source of heavy rare earths.
insights.locator: In August, ex-China heavy rare earths rose

insights.claim: China's government is due to update its rare earth export restrictions when the current controls expire in November 2026, a key price catalyst for Q4.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The November decision is a binary event for the ex-China heavy rare earth premium: tighter controls would widen it, while relaxed controls could compress it.
insights.locator: What could impact rare earths prices in Q4?

insights.claim: Buyers report little success exporting ytterbium and erbium from China in recent months, even though these elements are not currently under export controls. This suggests informal restrictions that go beyond the official control list.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Chinese supply risk reaches elements that are not on the official control list, so scarcity premiums could spread to other minor rare earths.
insights.quote: Buyers speaking to Benchmark have already indicated they have had little luck exporting ytterbium and erbium from China in recent months, even though these minerals are not currently under export controls

insights.claim: In North America and Europe, demo- and pilot-scale buying by aspiring magnet makers is likely to push heavy rare earth oxide prices higher in Q4 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: New Western magnet capacity adds heavy rare earth demand before new supply arrives, which supports a further rise in ex-China DyTb prices into Q4.
insights.quote: demo- and pilot-scale procurement from aspiring magnet makers is likely to drive up heavy rare earth oxide prices
